rows.description: Being scolded in front of the whole class makes me want to vanish. It is not my fault that an adult chose to shame me; I can tell a parent or another teacher what happened.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, guilt, trust
related mind states: shame, humiliation

rows.description: When I was punished unfairly, I still told my parent the whole story. Trusting them to listen helps them see the truth and shows me that not every adult will misjudge me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, guilt, humiliation
related mind states: trust

rows.description: Adults decide, and I cannot argue back, which feels helpless. Naming that feeling to someone safe and asking to be heard politely is better than swallowing it or taking revenge.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, guilt, humiliation, trust
related mind states: trust

rows.description: My classmate was punished for something she didn't do, and I know the truth. Speaking up quietly for her, even when it is scary, is a brave and kind thing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, guilt, humiliation, trust
related mind states: empathy

rows.description: The teacher later admits she was wrong. I feel relieved but still a bit sore. Accepting a sincere apology teaches me that adults are human, and forgiving gently frees me from carrying the anger.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, humiliation, trust
related mind states: anger, relief, regret

rows.description: My parents punish me before hearing my side, and I shout that it isn't fair. Sharing my feelings once calmly, after cooling down, is more likely to be heard than protest in the heat of the moment.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, guilt, humiliation, trust
related mind states: calm

rows.description: I dread showing the mark sheet because I imagine my parents' disappointment. Sharing the result early with a calm plan helps more than hiding the paper, which only grows the fear.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, envy, pride, shame
related mind states: disappointment, fear, calm

rows.description: My parents beam and tell everyone about my marks. I feel happy but also pressure to do it again. It helps to enjoy their joy while remembering that my worth is more than my rank.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, envy, fear, shame
related mind states: joy, pride

rows.description: My parents sigh over my marks and compare me to a cousin. I feel small. It is not my fault they are anxious; I can say I will try harder and ask for help without losing my self-respect.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, fear, pride, shame
related mind states: admiration, disappointment, anxiety

rows.description: My friend topped the class and I feel a sting in my stomach. It is normal; asking what helped him study turns envy into learning, while running him down only hurts us both.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, fear, pride, shame
related mind states: envy, hurt
